newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on speculation, peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on speculation, peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended up 50 basis points at 19.00 percent on Thursday due to what fixed-income analysts said was speculative ahead of potential short-term tripwires for the market.

"Although macroeconomic data have been good for the market, there is still uncertainty over the mid-term elections (on July 6) and the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting (on July 2)," one analyst said.
Another analyst said secondary rates had gained due to late weakness on the peso.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 4.1 centavos weaker at 7.9430/7.9460 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 484 million pesos from the market through two repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper mirrored government rates and ended up 50 basis points at 19.75 percent.
Liquidity of 10.188 billion pesos was due to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
